title: Drop DEBUG logs from payment-service
explanation: Payment service DEBUG logs account for ~35% of total log volume (1.24M records/day). No queries, dashboards, or alerts referenced these logs in the past 30 days. Dropping DEBUG logs while keeping INFO, WARN, and ERROR retains all critical operational context.

title: Drop GET /healthz spans from frontend
explanation: Kubernetes readiness and liveness probes execute GET /healthz every 250ms, producing 345k spans per day (25% of total trace volume). These health spans are never queried in incident investigations or dashboards.

rule.config_yaml:
processors:
  filter/healthz:
    traces:
      span:
        - attributes["http.target"] == "/healthz" and attributes["http.status_code"] == 200

title: Deduplicate repeated exception stacks in cart
explanation: The cart service catches Redis timeout errors and re-logs identical 45-line stack traces 3 times across nested handlers. Retaining only the initial exception log eliminates redundant storage without losing error diagnostics.

title: Convert inventory heartbeat logs to metrics
explanation: Worker threads emit periodic heartbeat strings every second (864k logs/day). Aggregating these events into a count metric preserves worker liveness visibility while avoiding raw log ingestion.

title: Drop high-cardinality user.id metric dimension
explanation: Metric http.server.request.duration contains high-cardinality dimension user.id (100k+ series). Dashboards and alerts aggregate exclusively by service.name and http.route.

title: Redact customer email addresses in email-service logs
explanation: Transactional email logs leak unmasked customer email addresses. Redacting email patterns preserves delivery audit logging while ensuring GDPR/privacy compliance.

rule.matcher: matchesValue(dt.service.name, "email") and matchesPhrase(content, "Sent confirmation to user:")
